task.description: Produce the design artefact (lib/letflow/design/req182-webhooks-routes.md or similar) for REQ-182: a new lib/letflow/routers/webhooks.ex router exposing GET /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions (list, response {items: [WebhookSubscription]}), POST /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions (create, response body must include hmac_secret_once when present), PATCH /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions/:id (update, accepting {status: ...} or {is_active: ...} per REQ-181's already-shipped reconciliation), DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions/:id (delete). All four gated by the WebhooksManage permission (REQ-069's matrix -- verify the real policy-key/permission mapping in lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex, do not assume it mirrors DlqOperate's role set). Cross-tenant/nonexistent ids must both fold to 404 (never 403 beyond the initial permission check), matching REQ-178's precedent and REQ-072's INV-5 rule. WebhookSubscription JSON serialization must match web/src/types/api.ts field-for-field (target_url, event_types, status, created_at at minimum) and must NEVER include the hashed secret or any secret-shaped field except hmac_secret_once, and only on the create response. Design must specify: (1) exact route definitions and how each maps params to lib/letflow/webhooks.ex's real create/2, list/1, update/3, delete/2 signatures; (2) the JSON serialization allowlist; (3) the permission-check mechanism and confirmed role set; (4) the cross-tenant-404 mechanism (inherited from the context module's tenant-schema scoping, same as REQ-178); (5) the moduledoc's explicit disclosure that R-Co's webhooks.zig was not inspected and web/src/api/dlq.ts + web/src/types/api.ts were the binding contract instead. Design only -- no fenced code blocks reproducing real .ex content (this project's mechanical no-exceptions rule, violated and caught on REQ-157/174/176/177/181's own design in this exact pipeline -- REQ-181 got reworked for exactly this mistake one run ago).
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions with no secret supplied returns a 2xx response whose body includes hmac_secret_once carrying the plaintext secret exactly once; a subsequent GET/list of the same subscription never includes the plaintext secret or an hmac_secret_once field at all -- two explicit tests
PATCH /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions/:id accepts {status: "PAUSED"} and, separately, {is_active: false}, and both result in a subscription that subsequently reads back as PAUSED via GET/list

every subscription route requires the WebhooksManage permission from REQ-069's matrix -- a caller lacking it receives 403, and a caller from a different tenant naming a real subscription id belonging to tenant A receives 404, never 403
GET /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions returns {items: [...]} with each item's target_url, event_types, status and created_at present, matching webhooksApi.list's consumer shape
DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions/:id removes the subscription such that a subsequent list no longer includes it, and a second DELETE of the same id returns 404 rather than a duplicate success

the route module's moduledoc states explicitly that R-Co's webhooks.zig was not inspected in this batch (unreachable from the drafting environment) and that web/src/api/dlq.ts / web/src/types/api.ts were the binding contract instead
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
